source_text: A 2011 systematic review and meta-analysis of case-control studies found men circumcised neonatally or in youth had an odds ratio of 0.33 (95% CI 0.13-0.83) for invasive penile cancer compared to uncircumcised men, attributing part of the effect to reduced human papillomavirus (HPV) persistence and chronic inflammation. [34]
